final_message:
I fixed the crash in `src/vunnel/providers/wolfi/parser.py`. `SecDBParser.build_reference_links` called `.extend()` on the shared helper's result, and that helper returns `None` for ids that aren't `CVE-` or `GHSA-` prefixed. It now treats `None` as an empty list. So `build_reference_links("GO-2026-5932")` returns just `[f"{parser.security_reference_url}/GO-2026-5932"]`, and CVE ids keep their current links.

I didn't check how chainguard gets its parser. I only ran the existing wolfi and chainguard unit tests, which pass (16 passed). I didn't add a test for the `GO-` id, and I didn't run the full suite or mypy.

`answer.json` is written in the repository root with the one-sentence summary.

steps.command: cd src/vunnel/providers; sed -n 60,95p wolfi/parser.py; sed -n 65,90p secureos/parser.py; grep -n "def build_reference_links" -A25 ../utils/vulnerability.py; grep -rn "build_reference_links" chainguard minimos

cd /tmp/bsvc-bliqat3t/vunnel && python3 - <<'E'
p='src/vunnel/providers/wolfi/parser.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("        urls.extend(vulnerability.build_reference_links(vulnerability_id))\n        return urls","        urls.extend(vulnerability.build_reference_links(vulnerability_id) or [])\n        return urls",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
git diff --stat; grep -rn "SecDBParser" src | head -3
echo '{"summary": "Wolfi/chainguard SecDBParser.build_reference_links now tolerates ids without CVE-/GHSA- prefix, falling back to only the distro security page link."}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/unit/providers/wolfi tests/unit/providers/chainguard 2>&1 | tail -3; grep -n "class SecDBParser" -B3 src/vunnel/providers/chainguard/*.py | head
